w: Founded by the 2004 World Barista Champion, the tiny Gruners gate bar roasts light Nordic-style single origins bought direct from producers. Ranked number two on the World's 100 Best Coffee Shops 2026 list, it still draws pilgrims for pour-overs and its upstairs microroastery.
s: Nordic light-roast pioneer, ranked world No.2 cafe
why: Founder-roaster is a former world champion; ranked #2 globally in 2026

w: Co-founded in 2007 by 2006 World Barista Champion Klaus Thomsen, the Jaegersborggade cafe anchors a direct-trade roastery with eight Copenhagen locations. Beans are bought at origin with published prices, and its light Nordic roasts helped define Scandinavian third-wave coffee.
s: Direct-trade roaster co-founded by a world champion
why: Founder is a world barista champion; benchmark Nordic third-wave roaster

w: Tucked into the San Benito district, this sensory coffee lab was founded by barista coach Federico Bolanos to showcase Salvadoran microlots through precise brewing and tasting flights. It placed third on the World's 100 Best Coffee Shops 2026 list, the highest ranking Central America has reached.
s: Salvadoran coffee lab ranked No.3 in the world
why: Ranked #3 worldwide in 2026, highest ever for Central America

w: A minimalist Selegie Road studio pouring precise single origins from Costa Rica, Rwanda and Kenya, it has been named Asia's best coffee shop two years running on the World's 100 Best Coffee Shops list, landing at number six overall in 2026, the only Singapore entry on the list.
s: Asia's top-ranked cafe, back to back
why: Best coffee shop in Asia two years running, #6 worldwide in 2026

w: Opened in late 2023 on Iakob Nikoladze Street in Vera, this roastery pairs Caucasian carpets with exposed concrete and roasts Guatemalan, Colombian and Ethiopian lots on site. It has quickly become a reference point for Georgia's fast-growing specialty scene, with a bakery counter attached.
s: Industrial-chic roastery reviving Tbilisi's cafes
why: Fast-rising flagship of Tbilisi's booming specialty coffee wave

w: Set on Pushkin Street, this was Yerevan's first dedicated specialty roastery, part of the Collective Group that helped seed the city's third-wave scene. State-of-the-art brewing gear and rotating single origins draw a growing crowd of Armenian coffee drinkers still discovering life beyond instant.
s: Armenia's first specialty coffee roastery
why: First specialty roastery in Armenia, still a scene anchor

w: Roasting specialty coffee in Riga for over eight years, Kalve runs several small Espresso Rooms across the city including its Stabu iela flagship, staffed by Q Grader certified baristas. It holds B Corp certification, a rare distinction for a coffee business in the Baltic states.
s: Q-grader roastery with five city espresso rooms
why: Latvia's leading B Corp-certified specialty roaster

w: Led by Emanuelis Ryklys, this Zverynas micro-roaster began roasting in 2011 and opened its cafe four years later, often cited as the best specialty coffee in the Baltics. Rotating single-origin filters and a relaxed roastery-attached bar keep Vilnius coffee regulars coming back.
s: The Baltics' most innovative micro-roaster cafe
why: Widely cited as the best specialty coffee shop in the Baltic states

w: Near Piata Charles de Gaulle, BOB Coffee Lab built its reputation on precise brewing and a rotating single-origin list, consistently rated among the highest-quality cups in the Romanian capital. The airy, plant-filled space doubles as a training ground for the city's next wave of baristas.
s: Scientific yet soulful, Bucharest's benchmark cup
why: Reference roaster credited with elevating Bucharest's coffee scene

w: Roasting on site in the leafy Vracar district, Lokal was recognized in the European Coffee Trip Awards 2025 for its careful sourcing and clean, balanced filter coffee. The small bar keeps a tight rotation of single origins alongside easy Serbian-style hospitality.
s: European Coffee Trip award winner in Vracar
why: European Coffee Trip Awards 2025 recognition

w: Housed within Ljubljana's City Museum on Gosposka ulica, Stow roasts its own beans and was singled out as a winning cafe in the European Coffee Trip Awards. Vaulted stone ceilings meet minimalist counters for one of Slovenia's most distinctive specialty coffee settings.
s: Award-winning roaster inside the City Museum
why: European Coffee Trip Award winner, Slovenia's top roaster

w: Founded by Ibrahim Al Mallouhi, this Dubai Design District flagship built its name on a scientific, precision-first approach to brewing and sourcing exceptional single-origin microlots. It has grown into one of the most cited names when locals debate the UAE's best specialty coffee.
s: Scientific coffee bar in Dubai Design District
why: One of the most acclaimed roasters driving Dubai's specialty scene

w: On a quiet street in the hillside Jabal Lweibdeh district, Dimitri's has roasted and brewed specialty coffee since 2014, blending European and Asian brewing trends. It anchors Amman's still-small but fast-growing specialty scene, with a shaded courtyard favored by artists and writers.
s: Jabal Lweibdeh institution since 2014
why: Long-running anchor of Amman's specialty coffee scene

w: Set in the Nairobi neighbourhood where one of Kenya's first coffee estates was planted in 1905, Spring Valley has roasted here since 2009 and just opened its first international cafe in London's Islington, winning Best New Coffee Shop at the 2026 London Coffee Festival Awards.
s: Roasting since 2009 where Kenyan coffee began
why: 2026 London Coffee Festival Best New Coffee Shop award winner

w: Run in partnership with Rwandan women coffee farmers, this Gishushu cafe channels profits back into grower training and offers cupping classes alongside its espresso bar. It has become Kigali's most cited specialty destination and a showcase for the country's rising Bourbon lots.
s: Women-farmer-owned coffee bar and roastery
why: Landmark grower-owned specialty coffee project, Kigali favorite

w: With six locations across Bogota including its Calle 70A roastery-cafe, Libertario roasts coffee from Colombia, Mexico and Costa Rica while pushing environmental sustainability in sourcing. It is a frequent pick for the city's best cup among Bogota's fast-growing specialty crowd.
s: Roasting Colombia's own beans across six cafes
why: One of Bogota's most-cited specialty roasters

w: On Orizaba street in Roma Norte, Buna helped anchor what became Latin America's densest specialty coffee cluster, roasting in house alongside a tight brunch menu. The corridor around it, including Almanegra and Cumbe, put Mexico City on the world specialty coffee map by the mid-2010s.
s: Roma Norte anchor of Mexico City's coffee cluster
why: Anchor cafe of Mexico City's dense Roma Norte coffee cluster

w: Roasting Peruvian beans since 1958, this Barranco institution on Pedro de Osma predates the third-wave movement by decades and is often called Lima's most famous coffee house. In-house cataors and Q Graders select and roast daily, championing Peru's still-underrated coffee origins.
s: Peru's best-known coffee house since 1958
why: Peru's most storied specialty roaster, running since 1958

w: Isabela Raposeiras, Brazil's first national barista champion, opened this Vila Madalena roastery-lab in 2004 as both cafe and barista school. Tasting flights walk drinkers through Brazilian terroir, and it remains a reference point for the country's specialty movement two decades on.
s: Founded by Brazil's first barista champion
why: Founded by Brazil's first barista champion; 20-year reference cafe

w: Near Phaya Thai BTS, Factory pairs an ambitious in-house roastery with a team of Thai baristas who have won multiple national and international coffee championships. Sleek industrial styling and barista training courses have made it a Ratchathewi destination for serious coffee travelers.
s: Barista world-champion team near Phaya Thai
why: Run by a team of national and world championship-winning baristas

w: Opened in 2023 down a small Hoan Kiem alley, VULAB is run by a pharmacist-turned-roaster holding SCA sensory and Q Grader credentials. Precise brew recipes and Vietnamese-grown specialty lots have quickly made it one of Hanoi's most talked-about new coffee openings.
s: Pharmacist-turned-Q-grader's precision coffee lab
why: Q-grader-run lab, one of Hanoi's most acclaimed 2023 openings

w: Among the most technically serious of Saigon's specialty roasters, Hoff built its reputation on an unusual obsession with brew water chemistry alongside careful sourcing of Vietnamese and imported beans. The District 1 flagship draws local coffee professionals as much as travelers.
s: Water-obsessed roaster-cafe in District 1
why: One of HCMC's most technically serious specialty roasters

w: Opened in a converted Mapo-gu building, Fritz Coffee Company built a cult following for its bold branding, in-house bakery and confidently dark-leaning roasts, becoming a reference point that reshaped how Seoul thinks about specialty coffee. It has since expanded citywide from this original base.
s: Cult roastery that reshaped Korean coffee culture
why: Widely credited with reshaping modern Seoul coffee culture

w: Hidden in a Menteng side street, Giyanti has roasted Indonesian single origins in house since 2012, championing small-lot Sumatran, Javanese and Sulawesi coffees before that was fashionable. It remains the elder statesman of Jakarta's now-crowded specialty coffee scene.
s: Menteng institution roasting Indonesia since 2012
why: Jakarta's pioneering single-origin roaster since 2012

w: Overlooking Albion Park, Fonzie Abbott has roasted specialty coffee since 2010 and later added an on-site beer brewery and spirits distillery, an unusual trifecta claimed to be unique worldwide. The industrial-chic space anchors Brisbane's inner-north coffee and craft-drink scene.
s: Roastery, brewery and distillery under one roof
why: Unique roastery-brewery-distillery combination, Brisbane landmark

w: Co-founded by six-time Canadian Barista Champion Ben Put, this Britannia flagship houses Monogram's roastery, training center and cafe. Precision espresso and rotating microlots have made it Calgary's most decorated specialty coffee name and a rising force in Canadian coffee competitions.
s: Flagship roastery of a six-time barista champion
why: Founder is a six-time Canadian Barista Champion

w: The Rogers flagship on East Walnut Avenue anchors Onyx's eight Northwest Arkansas locations, combining a full production roastery, barista training facility, bakery and cocktail bar. In 2026 it became the first American cafe ever named the World's Best Coffee Shop.
s: Named the world's best coffee shop in 2026
why: First-ever American winner of World's Best Coffee Shop, 2026

w: Founded by James Chen after he won the Nordic Roaster Competition as its first non-Nordic entrant, Fika Fika roasted the coffee that carried Berg Wu to Taiwan's first World Barista Championship title in 2016. The Zhongshan cafe remains a pilgrimage stop for Taipei coffee fans.
s: Nordic-style roaster behind a world champion's beans
why: Roasted the beans behind Taiwan's first World Barista Champion

w: On the corner of Bree and Shortmarket downtown, Rosetta's flagship cafe has been named Best Roastery in South Africa three times and drawn mentions among the world's best specialty coffee shops from the Financial Times. Directly sourced African and Latin American lots headline the rotating menu.
s: Three-time Best Roastery in South Africa
why: Three-time Best Roastery in South Africa, internationally noted

w: Opened on Emmanouil Mpenaki street in 2009, Taf effectively launched the Athens third-wave coffee movement. Founder Yiannis Taloumis is a licensed Q Grader who built Europe's first Q Lab, and head barista Stefanos Domatiotis won the 2014 World Brewers Cup brewing on this very bar.
s: Athens third-wave pioneer since 2009
why: Founder built Europe's first Q Lab; staff won 2014 World Brewers Cup
